commitTitle: feat(config): add the schema validation view with error mapping and the JSON-Schema-Test-Suite
summary: I built stage F, the schema validation view, in internal/config/schemaview. Compile builds the rendered view once per apiVersion with jsonschema/v6. It uses draft 2020-12 and leaves formats and content keywords as annotations. Its loader refuses every URL; a remote $ref fails with ErrSchema and keeps ErrRemoteReference in the error chain. A Ruralz vocabulary, asserted on every schema object, checks the shapes of the seven x-ruralz-* keywords, rejects any other x-ruralz-* keyword, and parses them into Schema.Extensions. Each kind's definition is compiled once. Embedded and Set serve the compiled views by apiVersion. View.Validate and Set.Validate check one tree.Resource and map every error to a sorted diag.List at a key-aware diag.Path, with positions from the FileTable; a node without a position points at its parent. The mapping covers 01 req 33: RZ-CFG-006 for each unknown member, at its key, with a nearest-name hint and the dedicated namespace, status and $patch messages. RZ-CFG-005 covers enum (with a nearest-value hint), required (at the parent), type (every allowed type in schema order, plus a hint to quote a plain scalar), and the generator's exactlyOneOf, atLeastOneOf and atMostOneOf, which name their fields. For anyOf, the reported cause is the branch that matches the instance's type. Duration, ByteSize and Decimal failures use the documented syntax text. Messages for the OTLP endpoint, metadata.name and a few hash and code fields are chosen by schema location, not by regex (CR 145). RZ-CFG-012 is reported once per secret field and never contains a value or any member name below the field. The package also reports duplicate keyed-list entries and set elements at the second entry, with the first as the related location (01 req 34), and reserved ruralz.io/ label and annotation keys (01 req 35). I vendored the JSON-Schema-Test-Suite with scripts/update-test-suites.sh json-schema (commit 5b0ee16, SHA-256 checked). An integration-tagged runner passes all 1,301 draft2020-12 cases (46 files, no optional/ files) through the production compiler configuration, with remotes/ preloaded in memory. The meta test checks both schema files, every $ref and definition, all ten kinds, the dispatch of all 23 Policy types, the vocabulary's shape checks, and that the vocabulary and schemaidx parse the same keyword values. The one part I could not do is loading the examples/ Bundles in the meta test (see requirements).

The rendered view uses neither keyword, so schemaview is not affected. WP-51 should not trust InstanceLocation for those error kinds; 07 req 18 already limits the detail to the keyword location.

For WP-69 (pipeline): call schemaview.Embedded(schemaidx set) once per process and share the *Set across workers; it is immutable and was tested concurrently under -race. WP-69 (pipeline): schemaview.View.Validate now returns at most schemaview.MaxDiagnostics (10,000) diagnostics per resource, the first in diag.List.Sort order. A resource that returns exactly MaxDiagnostics may have had more. The pipeline must treat reaching 10,000 as the 01 req 50 cap and append RZ-CFG-001 'too many diagnostics'.

Spec 01 req 6 owner / WP-33: MaxDocumentTokens covers YAML documents only, so a 64 MiB JSON document can still hold millions of members. schemaview's own mapping is now bounded, but jsonschema/v6 still builds one error per offending member before mapping. Consider applying the token or node limit to JSON documents too (an OQ for the configuration-model owner).

schemaidx owner: tree.Node.Get, schemaidx.Node.Select (a Get per dispatch case) and schemaidx.ItemElem (a Get or canonical JSON per element) scan linearly. schemaview now caches them for large objects, but other stage packages that call them once per element of one large object will hit the same quadratic pattern. Separately, schemaidx still accepts x-ruralz-since 0, x-ruralz-secret false and duplicate impact classes, which the vocabulary now rejects; aligning them is optional.

WP-01 (internal/config/diag), with an OQ on 01 req 48 (proposed OQ-configuration-model-N 'Bound on rendered path elements'): Path.String renders a keyed entry's key and a set element's canonical JSON in full in every diagnostic below them. diag.List.Sort calls Path.String in its comparator, so it re-renders both paths on every comparison, and WriteText and WriteJSON print them once per diagnostic. With up to 10,000 diagnostics under one 250 KB set element, text output alone is about 2.5 GB, and Collector.List or Sort renders far more than that. Proposed options: (a) above N bytes (for example 256), render an ElemKeyed key or ElemItem value in a bounded form, such as its list index '[<index>]' or a truncated JSON prefix with a length and hash marker, in both the human and JSON forms; (b) make List.Sort compare paths element by element, comparing the rendered text of each element against the other once, instead of rendering the whole path per comparison. Option (a) changes 01 req 48 and needs the OQ row; option (b) is internal to diag.

WP-28 (internal/config/schemaidx): if WP-01 picks option (a), ItemElem (and Cursor paths from Walk) should produce the same bounded element, so every stage names a large element the same way. Separately, an optional cheap accessor such as Node.Secret() bool, or Node.Keyword checks that do not clone Keywords, would let callers test x-ruralz-secret without copying CEL variables and Validations. Today schemaview works around this with a per-call cache keyed by schema node, so the accessor is not blocking.
deviations: The JSON-Schema-Test-Suite runner carries //go:build integration, so it runs in stage 8 (make integration) as 11 req 18 places it, not in make test. R-31 only says 'schemaview tests'.

No optional/ suite file is run, because Ruralz asserts no format: 01 req 32 has formats not asserted, the rendered view uses none, and 07 req 75 keeps format an annotation. usedFormats() is the one place to add a format if Ruralz ever asserts one. format.json in the main directory, which tests the annotation behavior, passes.
There is no JSON skip list: refRemote cases are not skipped. The runner preloads data/remotes/ with AddResource, and the production compiler keeps its refusing loader, as CR 134 allows.

RZ-CFG-012 is reported once per x-ruralz-secret field, at the field's path and position. It covers literals and also malformed secretRef objects below the field (bad provider enum, empty name, unknown members). Its reasons are worded from schema member names only, never authored keys or values, so a secret typed as a member name cannot leak. 01 req 33 names only the literal and extra-member cases.

A resource whose kind the view does not dispatch is validated against the root schema. The finding is RZ-CFG-005 at kind with a nearest-kind hint, not RZ-CFG-007, because stage F raises only 005, 006 and 012 and stage C already reports RZ-CFG-007.
The ruralz.io/ prefix check (01 req 35) is case-insensitive, as DNS prefixes are, so a key such as Ruralz.IO/x cannot get around the reservation.

Enum messages list the allowed values only for enums of 12 values or fewer; for longer enums (PolicyType has 23) they rely on the nearest-value hint. No message repeats the authored value, because the diagnostic position already shows it.

Beyond what CR 145 asks, syntax text selected by schema location is also used for $defs/Decimal, ObjectMeta.name, APIKey.hash, BasicCredential.hash, Pricing.currency and $defs/CountryCode, in place of the raw regex.

The regression tests' fixed budget is counted work, not wall-clock time. Each document may cost at most 16 members or elements read per node, counted by the memo. The repository rules (.claude/rules/go-code.md, Tests) forbid tests that depend on wall-clock time. BenchmarkValidateLarge reports the timings. The counter only catches a broken cache: a change that bypassed the memo entirely and called tree.Node.Get, Select or ItemElem directly would not be counted.

Truncation keeps the first MaxDiagnostics in sorted order rather than stopping after a number of errors. jsonschema/v6 reports a large object's errors in Go map order, so stopping early would keep a different set on each run, against 01 req 50's identical-diagnostics rule. The mapper keeps at most 2x the cap: it sorts, keeps the cap, and drops later entries that sort after the last one kept.

The fix goes beyond the finding's two hot spots. It also caches schemaidx.Node.Select and schemaidx.ItemElem for large objects and list elements, which were per-error linear scans too (a 20k-member Policy spec with 20k config errors took 47 s). It also computes nearest-name hints only for kept diagnostics, and deduplicates secret reasons as they arrive so a large secret subtree stays bounded.

duplicateKeys compares keys by canonical JSON (schemaidx.AppendItemJSON) rather than by kind plus text. Like set elements, "1" and 1 are different keys while 1 and 1.0 are the same key, which is how the canonical form will identify entries. A numeric key appears unquoted in the message.

The not recognizer now requires required-only pairs. `not: {required: [a, b, c]}` means 'not all three' and is not schemagen output; it now gets the generic message instead of being misworded as 'at most one of'.

The x-ruralz-ref enum hardcodes the ten kinds of foundation pack section 3; TestMetaDispatch checks it equals the root dispatch. The backstop keyword parser now also rejects since 0 and secret false, to match the meta-schema.

Fix part (2) of finding 2, validating raw YAML through WP-33's profile, is not done because internal/config/profile is still untracked and being edited this wave. It is forwarded as a contract request.

Minor finding: the suggested fix was to build the path once per locate call, with capacity len(loc), and append in place. I went further: every distinct location prefix is resolved once per Validate, in a trie of steps that each hold the position, path node and text, so later errors at or below a position allocate nothing in locate. The Keywords().Secret check is cached per schema node inside the memo instead of adding a schemaidx accessor, so no contract change is needed; the accessor is filed only as an optional request.

The allocation budget in TestLargePathElements is 1024 bytes per input byte, not something tighter. Measured mapping is 222-325 B per input byte, including the diag.Nearest matrix the contract allocates for each kept hint. Code that renders the path per diagnostic needs 12,000-50,000 B per input byte on these inputs, so the budget still separates the two by more than 10x. The test also requires that doubling the errors at most triples the allocations.
The OQ row for 01 req 48 is not written into .claude/plans/m1/specs/01-config-load.md, because that file is outside the WP-35 owned paths; its proposed text is in contractRequests.

commitTitle: feat(config): add overlay merge and environment substitution
summary:
I built stage D (internal/config/overlay) and stage E (internal/config/subst) of the configuration pipeline. There was no earlier attempt to recover.

**overlay**
- `Apply(base, patches, Options)` merges one overlay into the base with Kubernetes strategic-merge rules, reading list types from the schema through schemaidx.
- Objects merge recursively and an overlay null removes a member. Scalars and removals are applied first, so a Policy config is merged under the merged spec.type.
- map and orderedMap lists merge by key, support `$patch: delete`, and append new entries. An orderedMap list can be reordered with a first `{$patch: replace}`. set and atomic lists are replaced.
- The JSONSchemaDocument value is replaced whole and nothing inside it merges (CR 144/161).
- The `ruralz.io/patch` annotation supports delete and replace and is always removed. Malformed directives are RZ-CFG-005, `$patch` in a base document is RZ-CFG-006, and patch identity conflicts are RZ-CFG-008 / RZ-CFG-030.
- An identity declared twice in one overlay is reported and neither copy is applied. New resources come out in (kind, name) order, so the result does not depend on file order.
- A small `Selection` type covers req 23: the overlay directory, which files belong to it, and RZ-CFG-009 for an explicit spec.overlay with no directory.

**subst**
- `New(Options).Apply(res)` implements the `${VAR}` / `${VAR:-default}` / `$${` grammar, substitutes once and never re-scans, and records the variables used in `Node.Vars`.
- A scalar that is exactly one expression is re-typed by the schema (integer, number, boolean, ByteSize, IntOrString).
- Forbidden positions give RZ-CFG-011 and nothing else for that scalar. Policy dispatch is applied after spec.type is substituted.
- Undefined variables are RZ-CFG-010, one per occurrence, with a nearest-name hint when the source is an Environment. Malformed expressions are RZ-CFG-005.
- It owns both RZ-CFG-013 warnings, as architecture 3.1 assigns: secret-like variable names, and credential-shaped values (nine pattern detectors plus a literal value for a credential header in a headers `set[]` entry).
- `Escape` and `Environ` are provided for render and for the process environment.

**Tests**
- Schema-driven tests walk every field from the committed schema: all 53 list fields are merged by their list type, and on all 288 string fields subst agrees with `schemaidx.Info` on forbidden positions and secret subtrees.
- `FuzzOverlay` checks determinism, idempotence, that no directive survives, and that every code is registered.
- `FuzzSubst` is property P3: substitution never changes tree shape, and its text matches an independent regex reading of the grammar; it also checks the `Escape` round trip.
- `TestResultIndependentOfFileOrder` is property P5: every ordering and file split of the overlay gives the same result.
- Both packages have a `BenchmarkApply`.
requirements: Implemented: 01 F 23 (overlay directory, file membership and RZ-CFG-009 for an explicit missing overlay, in overlay.Selection; finding and reading the files stays with the loader, WP-55), F 24 (RZ-CFG-008 within one overlay across one or two files, RZ-CFG-030, unserved apiVersion is RZ-CFG-007 only), F 25 (the whole merge table, directive validation, RZ-CFG-006 for $patch in a base document, result nodes keep the position of the document that supplied them), G 26 (grammar, RZ-CFG-005), G 27 (substitute once, never on keys, not recursive, :- treats empty as unset, RZ-CFG-010 per occurrence with an Environment-only hint), G 28 (forbidden positions report RZ-CFG-011 only; $${ is still unescaped there), G 29 (re-typing for integer, number, boolean, ByteSize, IntOrString; partial substitution or a value that does not fit stays a string, with Vars set), G 30 (RZ-CFG-013 for secret-like names), G 31 (subst.Escape; the profile.Encode side belongs to WP-33), and the 01 J row-013 credential-literal detectors that architecture 3.1 assigns to this stage. CR 144/161 implemented and tested. Fuzz targets FuzzOverlay and FuzzSubst, property P3 (substitution never injects structure) and P5 (result independent of file order) are present and pass. Nothing in scope is left unimplemented.

contractRequests: The specs disagree on $${ in forbidden positions, and render will not round-trip unless the lead picks one rule. 01 req 28 says $${ is still unescaped there and 01 req 31 says profile.Encode writes every literal ${ back as $${. But 02 req 46 and the schemaidx Info.NoSubstitution doc comment ("render writes no $${ escape (02 req 46)") say render writes no escape in those positions, and 02 test 19 expects a "verbatim ${ in a CEL field". subst follows 01 and CM "Overlays" ("it writes a literal ${ that came from a $${ escape back as $${"). So if WP-58/WP-33 skip escaping in CEL, ref or secret fields, a CEL field authored with $${ renders as ${ and fails with RZ-CFG-011 on the next load. Recommended: render escapes every literal ${ in every string; drop the render clause from the NoSubstitution comment; reword 02 test 19 as "$${ in a CEL field round-trips". The other choice is to keep 02 and stop unescaping in forbidden positions, which changes 01 req 28.

For WP-55 (loader): overlay.Apply takes ownership of its inputs (it rewrites trees in place) and must run even when no overlay is selected (nil patches), because it is where the RZ-CFG-006 check for $patch in base documents runs. Build one subst.Substituter per load (it compiles the detectors once and is safe for concurrent use) and call Apply per resource; set diag Environment on the results yourself in multi-Environment runs. overlay.Selection, ValidName and Root cover req 23 and the spec.overlay name rule of req 21.

WP-03 (internal/config/schemaidx), for R-3: export either the undispatched schema of a Walk position (for example `Cursor.Static() *Node`) or a public step (for example `Info.Step(sel *Node, elem diag.PathElem, typedMapValue bool, parentDepth int, parentName string) Info`). config/subst could then take InSecret and NoSubstitution from schemaidx instead of its own copy in walk.go place.step. Today TestPositionsFromSchema is the mandatory cross-check that keeps the two in sync.

Spec 01 owner, an OQ against 01 req 25 and 27 (ordering gap): overlays merge before substitution. A dispatch member holding `${VAR}` (Policy spec.type) therefore selects no if/then branch, and spec.config merges as free content: keyed lists such as auth.jwt issuers are replaced whole instead of merged by key, the JSONSchemaDocument value merges member by member, and any `$patch` inside is RZ-CFG-005. Proposed options: (a) add Policy spec.type (dispatch members) to the 01 req 28 forbidden positions (RZ-CFG-011); (b) report RZ-CFG-005 at stage D when an overlay merges composite members under an unresolved dispatch member; (c) keep the free-content merge and document it in CM "Overlays". The current code does (c) and pins it in TestUnresolvedDispatch.

WP-55 (loader), interface note: `overlay.Apply` is now `Apply(ctx, base, patches, opts) ([]*tree.Resource, diag.List, error)` and no longer checks base documents. The loader must call `overlay.CheckBase(res, opts)` on every base resource in its worker pool, whether or not an overlay is selected. Apply returns ctx.Err() and no result on cancellation.
deviations: The API differs from the sketch in spec 01 section 3, following architecture R-3 (navigation through schemaidx, not schemaview). overlay.Apply(base, patches []*tree.Resource, Options{Schemas *schemaidx.Set, Files *tree.FileTable}) returns ([]*tree.Resource, diag.List) instead of mutating a map. subst is New(Options{Schemas, Files, Variables, HintNames}).Apply(res) instead of a free Apply(res, view, src, hints). Both take a FileTable so diagnostics carry file locations.
Fuzz targets are named FuzzOverlay and FuzzSubst as in the work package entry, not FuzzOverlayMerge and FuzzSubstitute as in spec 01 section 6.

Choices where the spec is silent: (a) $patch counts as a directive only in an object the schema describes; inside free content (undeclared members of open configs, the JSONSchemaDocument value) it is data, in both base and overlay documents. (b) Two overlay entries with one key in a single keyed list are RZ-CFG-005 at the second, related to the first, mirroring req 34. (c) An overlay entry merges into the first base entry with its key, and $patch: delete removes every base entry with that key. (d) ruralz.io/patch: replace with no spec in the overlay leaves the resource with no spec. (e) An overlay scalar equal to the base scalar keeps the base node and its position. (f) subst reports RZ-CFG-011 instead of RZ-CFG-007 when ${ appears in apiVersion or kind. (g) The literal-header credential detector covers headers set[] entries only, as the 01 J row states, not add[] entries.

Finding 5 (R-3): I took the finding's fallback of a comment rather than switching to schemaidx.Walk. Walk's Cursor exposes neither the undispatched schema (subst needs DispatchValues to substitute spec.type before the object's dispatch is read) nor a step for a member visited ahead of its siblings. Calling Lookup per scalar would re-resolve every path from the root. walk.go now states that TestPositionsFromSchema is the mandatory cross-check, and the API gap is raised as a contract change request.

Finding 6: I chose to keep and document authored key values in paths rather than recompute them after substitution. A path built from substituted key or set-element text would put a variable's value, including a secret-like one, into an RZ-CFG-013 diagnostic. Authored values also match the overlay stage's paths. The file, line and column still locate the node. This is documented on Substituter.Apply and pinned by TestPathsUseAuthoredKeys.

Finding 9: I raised a contract change request instead of adding a new stage D diagnostic, because spec 01 does not define this case and an error would block input the spec allows. The behavior is documented in the overlay package doc and pinned by TestUnresolvedDispatch.

Finding 2: I applied the primary fix (skip the header-literal check when Vars is set or the scalar is unresolved). I did not route the per-use secret-like warning through the per-scalar dedupe, because 01 req 30 requires one warning at each use. A secret-like variable whose value is itself credential-shaped still gets both the name warning and the detector warning. These report two different facts.

remainingMinor.where: internal/config/overlay/merge.go:183-227 (mergeMap dispatch) and overlay.go:171-176; 01 req 25; FuzzOverlay property
remainingMinor.issue: A base `$patch` can still reach a clean result with no diagnostic. A base Policy of type validation.json-schema may legally hold `$patch` as data inside config.schema, and CheckBase rightly exempts it. An overlay that changes only spec.type to an open config type, such as `{"spec":{"type":"cors"}}` or `plugin`, moves that value into free content. The result keeps `$patch` at spec.config.schema.$patch and Apply reports nothing. FuzzOverlay's own properties fail on this reachable input: the second pipeline pass reports RZ-CFG-006, so the idempotency check fails, and strayPatch finds the member. I confirmed this with a probe that copies the fuzz body (base `{"kind":"Policy","spec":{"type":"validation.json-schema","config":{"schema":{"$patch":1}}}}`, overlay `{"spec":{"type":"cors"}}`). A 90 s fuzz run did not hit it, but nightly long runs can.
remainingMinor.fix: After merging an existing resource in Apply, check the merged tree for `$patch` outside a JSONSchemaDocument value. Report RZ-CFG-005, for example at the overlay spec.type, with a message saying the base value is no longer a JSON Schema document. CheckBase's walk can be reused on the merged root with a CodeSchema code.
